note: Two adjudicated readings of substance. Both witnesses spell the Virgin's title genitrix where this edition keeps genetrix throughout, and the hand missal declines the name of her spouse where witness do and this edition leave it indeclinable. Everything else is the orthography of the two declared classes, generated by checks/house_rules; witness handmissal-tlm collates under the substantive-only profile, so no accidental is compared against it.

adjudicated.ruling: Genetríce, against both witnesses, by the corpus's standing ruling. Genetrix is the older form of the same noun from gigno and genitrix the one that spread later; the dictionaries head both and neither page is wrong. The 1962 typical edition prints Genetrice in the Canon and in Libera nos and nowhere Genitrice, so this edition keeps that spelling throughout — which the ruling at ordinarium.libera-nos w020 already recorded, noting that witness do itself sets Genitríce in these prayers after Mass.

Ioseph, indeclinable, with witness do and with this edition's own reading of the name in the Canon (ordinarium.communicantes w021). Latin took the Hebrew name in twice: Ioseph stands unchanged in every case, and Iosephus declines as a second-declension noun, so a page may set either here and both are the man's name in the ablative. This is a difference of grammar rather than of spelling, which is why it is ruled under its own class and counted apart; the token is marked disputed so that it reaches the list an expert reviews.

The j-form against this edition's i-form, by the house rule in ORTHOGRAPHY.md. This edition prints i because the books it edits do: the 1962 typical edition sets Iesu, Ioánnem, iube and maiestátis throughout, and so does the Mszał Rzymski of the Tyniec Benedictines (Pallottinum, Poznań 1963), which is the book a Polish reader is most likely to hold. The mid-century hand missals print j; neither spelling is a different word, and the apparatus records theirs.

Beátis, with witness do's own setting of the word everywhere else — beáto stands five words earlier in this same line, accented. The a of beatus is long and takes the stress in every form of it; the missing accent here is this file's, on one word, and the reading is identical.
